instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice and get it cooking first.
Slice the 1.25 lb chicken thighs into thin, bite size pieces and toss them with 1/4 tsp salt.
Slice the bell pepper into thin strips. Cut the scallions on a slant into 1 inch pieces, using the light and dark green parts. Mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Finely chop 1/3 cup peanuts and chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro. Cut one lime into wedges. Thinly slice the 2 chilies into a small bowl for the table.
Heat the 1 1/2 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium. Add the pepper and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often, until it's soft and starting to brown.
Add the scallions and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until they soften. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds. Don't let it brown.
Add 2 1/2 tbsp curry paste and stir it into the vegetables for about 1 minute, until it darkens a little and smells fragrant.
Pour in the can of coconut milk and whisk in 2 tbsp fish sauce and 2 1/2 tbsp brown sugar. Bring it to a gentle boil, then turn it down and simmer for 2 minutes, until it's a little thicker.

Add the chicken and simmer, uncovered, for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Keep it at a gentle bubble, not a hard boil. You're cooking it to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut a thick piece open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Take the pan off the heat. Squeeze in 1 tbsp juice from the other lime and stir in the cilantro and peanuts.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or another squeeze of the lime.
Serve over the rice with the lime wedges, and the chilies on the side.
method_notes: Once Upon a Chef uses store-bought paste (red curry paste stands in for Panang), softens bell pepper, scallions and garlic, simmers the paste with coconut milk, fish sauce and brown sugar, poaches thin chicken in it for 5 to 8 minutes, then stirs in lime juice, cilantro and chopped peanuts. RecipeTin Eats makes its own Panang paste with ground peanuts and dried chillies, fries the paste for 5 minutes before any liquid, and finishes with Thai basil and green beans. This one follows the lead's ratios but fries the paste for a minute before the coconut milk, the way RecipeTin does, and uses thighs rather than the lead's breast so the chicken stays juicy.
